outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Procedural Posture and Factual Background
outline.description: This chapter establishes the narrative foundation of the case by detailing the emergency response to a domestic violence call, the specific interactions captured on body camera footage, and the procedural history from the initial entry to the appeal. It sets the stage for analyzing why the video evidence was crucial in resolving factual disputes regarding consent.
subtopics: The Emergency Context: Responding to a Domestic Violence Threat
Chronology of Events: Arrival, Initial Hesitation, and Entry
Key Body Camera Exchanges: The Dialogue Between Officer Kizer and Lisa Coleman
Discovery of Evidence: From Protective Sweep to Warrant Execution
Procedural History: Motion to Suppress, Magistrate Report, District Court Ruling, and Plea

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Legal Framework for Consent Searches
outline.description: This chapter outlines the governing Fourth Amendment principles applicable to third-party consent searches. It defines the legal standards for 'voluntariness' under the totality of circumstances test and clarifies the objective reasonableness standard used to determine the scope of consent.
subtopics: Consent as an Exception to the Warrant Requirement
Third-Party Authority: Validating Consent Given by Cohabitants (Matlock)
The Voluntariness Standard: Free and Voluntary Giving (Bumper v. North Carolina)
Totality of Circumstances Factors for Assessing Voluntariness
Scope of Consent: The Objective Reasonableness Standard (Florida v. Jimeno)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Analyzing Voluntariness Under Totality of Circumstances
outline.description: Focusing on the core legal battle, this chapter dissects how the Seventh Circuit applied the voluntariness factors to Officer Kizer's specific actions. It contrasts Coleman's argument regarding coercive language ('need') against the court's holistic view of tone, demeanor, prior refusal, and lack of custody.
subtopics: 'Need' vs. Command: Addressing Linguistic Ambiguity in Police Requests
Tone and Demeanor as Indicators of Non-Coercion
'Right to Refuse': Significance of Lisa's Initial Denial Followed by Subsequent Grant
Absence of Custody, Physical Coercion, or Prolonged Detention
'Clear Error' Review Standard Applied to Fact-Finding on Consent

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Determining Whether Officers Exceeded Scope of Consent
outline.description: This chapter examines whether the officers' actions inside the home remained within boundaries set by Lisa's verbal agreement. It explains how a 'protective sweep' based on child welfare concerns logically encompasses scanning rooms and locating individuals without constituting an unconstitutional general search.
subtopics: What Constitutes a Protective Sweep?
Defining Boundaries Based on Stated Purpose (Child Safety)
Reasonable Actions Within Scope: Locating Individuals and Asking Basic Questions
The Transition from Consensual Entry to Securing a Search Warrant

outline.description: Concluding observations on judicial deference in domestic violence scenarios and policy implications for law enforcement training. This chapter highlights why avoiding unnecessary doctrinal pivots (like exigent circumstances) strengthens rulings based squarely on consent.
subtopics: Judicial Deference to Trial Court Findings
Avoidance of Alternative Grounds (Exigent Circumstances/Inevitable Discovery)
Policy Implications for Offic er Conduct in High-Stress Domestic Calls
Significance of Video Evidence in Adjudicating Consent Cases
